accessibility: The status line and the record notes are status regions that announce changes; the Run Checks button is a real button that does not press while it runs.
A state is carried by its icon and its word, never by color alone; the error alerts are announced as alerts.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Rail, NavItem, Button, Stack, Text, Icon, Alert, EmptyState, Skeleton, SegmentedControl, Segment, TabBar and TabBarItem); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog. The shell is the one of the Overview View.

The strings of the app are copied under the same Locale keys, the plural ones one key per form; parameters are the Widget values ({value}, {value2}, {value3}). The Preview sources' View, Variant and Locale names, the run time and the Evidence digest are sample content. The sentence that names the sources that did not finish and the one that names why a run was not recorded are baked sample sentences (checks.sample.*), because the Widgets that show them take no translated parameter.
The spinning state icon of the real page is a static icon here: the Icon Widget has no spin.
The sources are Stack rows with one icon and one state text per state, only one visible, because a Widget cannot change its own icon or text; Variants choose the visible ones.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A member opened the Overview with ?tab=checks; the tab strip lists Views, Checks, Decisions, Requirements (only with a requirement source of the spec kind) and Activity, and Checks is the selected one. Opening the tab reads nothing and runs nothing.

The base state is a Workspace whose Checks have not run in this session: every source says "Not checked", the two Preview sources say that no Preview is open, and the list says Checks have not run. Variants show a run in progress, finished runs, an unfinished one and the errors and notes a run can raise.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the Workbench chrome follows the Workbench language, so its text is baked here per Locale. Time, counts, View and Variant names are sample content. The findings themselves are in Overview: Checks findings.
spec.intent: Show the Checks tab of the Overview as built from Adapter Widgets only: one Run Checks action, the state of every source a run reads, the Product Kit checks that a run starts, and what the list says before, during and after a run, so a person can tell a clean Workspace from one that was never checked.
interactionRules: Checks run only when asked: Run Checks reads every Workspace resource once and refreshes the whole result; it is the one primary action, and while it runs the button shows its progress and the status line says Checks are running.

Every source has its own state (Not checked, Checking…, Completed, Incomplete, Failed) with its finding count once it completed or was incomplete, so a source that has not run, is running or did not finish is never read as zero findings.

The sources are the Workspace's own structure and schema findings, translation reminders, Catalog problems of the entries a View uses, the Product Kit findings, and the open Preview's translation warnings and runtime errors; the Preview sources follow the Preview that is open, say which View they come from, and say so when that Preview is closed and the result may be out of date.

The Product Kit checks (registry, repeat capture, live versus fresh, props and emits) start with a run, report their own state each, and never block Preview, capture or Handoff; without the capture key they are not run and the row names the key.

A run with an unfinished source reads "No findings from the sources that completed" and names the sources that are not checked or not finished, never "clean"; a run whose sources all completed with no findings reads "No findings".

When a run has finished it is recorded as one new Evidence record, never replacing an earlier one; the line under the button says it is recording, where it was recorded, or why it was not (the capture key is missing, or the server could not store it).
A Workspace whose primary Locale has no file shows a persistent error with a link to Locales, and a resource that could not be read is named in its own error without stopping the others.
